spans.s:
√bhikṣ (bhíkṣate; bibhikṣé; bhikṣiṣyé;
bhíkṣitum; bhikṣitvā́). desire to have
a share for one's self, wish for; then (like
the Eng. desire, ‘express a wish for’), request;
 beg; esp. go begging for food.
[old desid. of √bhaj, 108g^1 end: cf.
bhakṣ.]

bhikṣā́, f.
 —1. the act of begging, begging;
 —2. that which is got by begging,
alms. [√bhikṣ, 1149^4: w. the relation of
1 to 2, cf. that of Eng. getting, ‘act of
getting,’ to getting, ‘that which is got.’]
